sources.citation: Ogden FL et al. (2017), The Soil Moisture Velocity Equation, JAMES 9
source_bound_findings: the finite moisture-content domain is discretized into fixed water-content bins
bins are binary filled/empty at a given depth rather than fractional spatial cells
the cited Talbot-Ogden accuracy requirement varies strongly by texture, from about 75 bins for clays to almost 400 for sands for deep well-drained infiltration
the reported forward-Euler explicit finite-volume solution requires timestep magnitude on the order of seconds during infiltration

sources.citation: Ogden FL et al. (2015), Validation of finite water-content vadose zone dynamics method using column experiments with a moving water table and applied surface flux
source_bound_findings: the moving-water-table validation used N=200 water-content bins
the paper notes that simpler groundwater-coupled infiltration schemes can use far fewer bins, but that statement is not evidence for the full FWC method under arbitrary SWAP forcing

sources.citation: Zhu J et al. (2016), An explicit approach to capture diffusive effects in finite water-content method for solving vadose zone flow, Journal of Hydrology 535:270-281
source_bound_findings: diffusive effects are added explicitly at the level of individual water-content bins
advection and diffusion are treated separately for each bin
the method improves water-content profile prediction but does not remove the bin-wise work structure

SWAP5_implications.reason: A production-credible accuracy range may require O(10^2) to O(4x10^2) bin states or equivalent compact front coordinates per hydraulic layer/material domain.
SWAP5_implications.multiswap_risk: Hundreds of bins combined with seconds-scale internal timesteps may produce predictable but still excessive throughput cost even without nonlinear iteration.
SWAP5_implications.memory_risk: Fixed bins avoid mathematically unbounded state growth, but multiple front/slug bookkeeping per bin must still be bounded explicitly.
SWAP5_implications.physics_policy_rule: Reducing bin count or enlarging internal timestep for throughput is a numerical approximation that requires explicit qualification against the reference and may not silently alter process physics.

required_next_tests: derive or reconstruct exact maximum front/slug objects per fixed-bin representation
measure accuracy-versus-bin-count for sand, clay, layered contrast and moving-water-table scenarios against FullRichards
measure accepted internal step count per forcing interval, including rainfall pulses and drying/re-wetting
separate FWC_ADVECTIVE and FWC_EXPLICIT_DIFFUSION cost envelopes
report persistent bytes per column, scratch bytes per worker, p50/p95/p99/max internal steps and branch/event counts
reject any production envelope whose worst-case cost cannot be bounded a priori or whose reduced bin count changes qualified physics beyond evidence-based limits
current_interpretation: FWC remains scientifically credible and mass-conservation-oriented, but its published discretization evidence weakens the hypothesis that it is automatically a low-state, low-cost MultiSWAP solver. Predictability and speed must be qualified separately.
